A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SymRTLO work. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–C support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting.

before.justification: Sections 2 and 4 report original FSM optimization, functional pass rates, wire/cell counts, PPA measurements, and component-ablation results.

after.justification: Retains these original experiments and reports additional PPA comparator results and an evaluation under stronger compiler settings.

M1.justification: Section 3.4 revises the stated verification procedure from SAT-based checking after testbench screening to circuit-dependent verification: SAT for simpler circuits and advanced sequential equivalence checking for asynchronous resets, CDC paths, or retimed logic. The dispatcher, retrieval, AST transformations, and FSM minimization approach remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same RTLRewriter coverage: 11 short wire/cell examples and 10 FSM/algorithm examples. The motivating FSM and appendix examples are retained. The benchmark counts move from Section 4.1 to 4.3; stronger compiler settings do not introduce new task coverage.

E2.justification: GPT-O1 gains reported comparisons in the FSM and algorithm PPA experiments, Tables 6–7, beyond its retained motivational use in Table 3. Table 6 also supplies explicit RTLRewriter entries for a comparison previously discussed in prose. Other comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4.3 adds evaluation using flattened mode with high mapping effort, beyond the retained medium-effort, incremental compiler configuration. Metrics and selection of the best of ten valid generations remain unchanged. The new token-cost discussion does not establish a changed sampling budget.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 adds a sensitivity check asking whether optimization gains persist under stronger compiler optimization. The component-removal ablations in Figure 5 and the FSM/AST examples in the appendices retain the same analyses and findings.

E5.justification: Neither version provides seed information, run-to-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The ten-generation sampling and pass@k reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 6 revises SymRTLO's example1 power/time/area from 0.047 mW, 0.36 ns, 534.4 µm² to 0.029 mW, 1.21 ns, 403.9 µm²; other isolated PPA entries also change. New comparator results and stronger-compiler results are added, the latter reporting 35.8% power, 0.5% delay, and 27.7% area improvements under that configuration. Tables 3–5 and Figure 5 retain their results.

T1.justification: V1's Section 3.3, Equation (9), explicitly formulates constrained FSM optimization by minimizing f(M', C) subject to data-path consistency. V2 removes this formulation and its explanation. Other mathematical definitions and retrieval equations remain, mostly converted to inline notation; no proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions, and conclusion retain the same novelty, data/control-flow optimization, verification, and performance claims, including the headline 43.9%, 62.5%, and 51.1% improvements. Additional comparisons support existing claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly describes the framework as model-agnostic and argues that the sampling comparison provides token-budget fairness. It replaces the earlier detailed discussion of SAT computational costs and verification tradeoffs with circuit-dependent verification applicability. Existing benchmark and RTLRewriter comparability limitations remain.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 adds Synopsys Formality for sequential verification and reports token consumption of 7,728 for SymRTLO versus approximately 775 per GPT-4o generation. It omits v1's explicit zero-area compiler constraint. Other toolchain details and the implementation examples in Appendices A–C are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds Chen et al.'s PyOD 2 reference to the neuro-symbolic/LLM background discussion. The prior-work taxonomy and novelty positioning otherwise remain unchanged; bibliographic reformatting does not constitute additional research-positioning changes.

P1.justification: Localized rewriting and sentence compression preserve the main section and appendix order. V2 removes the Impact Statement, relocates the benchmark-count description, updates title-page information, removes a duplicated author entry, and switches to numbered citations.

P2.justification: The two-column body becomes a single-column layout with extensive figure/table relocation and resizing, text wrapped around figures, reflowed appendix listings, and mostly inline equations. Tables 6–7 gain rows, and result highlighting changes from gray to yellow. Existing diagram and plot content is largely retained.

improvement.justification: The added GPT-O1 comparisons, explicit RTLRewriter results, and stronger-compiler check modestly strengthen the evidence supporting existing performance claims. Verifier and token-cost details also improve transparency. These gains are limited by aggregate-only reporting of the stronger-compiler test, unexplained numerical revisions, and removal of the explicit area-constraint setting.
